explanation: Arthur Conan Doyle created Moriarty for 'The Final Problem' (1893) so the two could plunge together over the Reichenbach Falls. Readers' dismay helped bring Holmes back in 1903.

claims.text: In Conan Doyle's stories, Sherlock Holmes calls Professor Moriarty 'the Napoleon of crime'.
Mycroft Holmes is Sherlock's brother, Lestrade a Scotland Yard detective and Colonel Moran Moriarty's chief henchman; Holmes calls none of them the Napoleon of crime.
Conan Doyle introduced Moriarty in The Final Problem, published in 1893, in which Holmes and Moriarty go over the Reichenbach Falls together.
Conan Doyle brought Holmes back in The Adventure of the Empty House in 1903, after readers' dismay at his apparent death.
